Canonical source: Albantakis et al. 2023, PLoS Comput Biol, 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011465
Distinctive signature Σ_T: Intrinsic cause-effect power; current-state interventional repertoires; intrinsic information; partition-based integration; exclusion/maximal complex; composition into distinctions/relations.
UCT-recoverable primitives: Mechanism-fixed responses; response differences; partitions/factorization; structural relations; declared max/min operations.
Required bridge B_T: IIT-compatible units/grain; TPM/intervention alignment; IIT reference prior; Intrinsic Difference metric; partition/max-min/tie conventions.
Strong target-theory claim preserved: Phenomenal existence/structure is tied to IIT cause-effect structure selected under IIT postulates, including exclusion.
Residual set R_T^res: IIT-specific phenomenal postulates; exclusion ontology; theory-specific neural/temporal empirical predictions; any ideal intervention not physically realizable.
Formal status F: computational F3; exclusion F0 under scoped overlap witness
Explicit fidelity-failure condition: Fail if IIT units/grain, repertoire definitions, prior/metric, partition rules or source-faithful exclusion claim are not preserved; F0 conflict is scoped to a still-realized lower UCT token excluded solely by overlap/nonmaximality.

Canonical source: Lamme 2006, Trends Cogn Sci, 10.1016/j.tics.2006.09.001; Lamme 2018 review
Distinctive signature Σ_T: Sensory/perceptual recurrent processing rather than feedforward sweep alone; content-sensitive recurrent interactions; theory-relevant timing; recurrence linked to conscious visual experience.
UCT-recoverable primitives: Directed causal graph; cycles/SCCs; loop delays; recurrent persistence; content-sensitive response dependence.
Required bridge B_T: Sensory/perceptual chart; content coordinate; neurobiological timing; stabilization/perceptual bridge.
Strong target-theory claim preserved: Recurrent processing between sensory/visual areas is central and, in strong formulations, sufficient for conscious visual experience.
Residual set R_T^res: Domain-specific neural timing/localization; sufficiency claim for visual phenomenology; empirical dissociations from attention/access.
Explicit fidelity-failure condition: Fail if recurrence is generic SCC only without sensory/content/timing/stabilization constraints, or if perceptual sufficiency is silently treated as recovered.

Canonical source: Dehaene & Changeux 2011, Neuron, 10.1016/j.neuron.2011.03.018; Mashour et al. 2020, Neuron
Distinctive signature Σ_T: Nonlinear ignition; recurrent amplification and sustained representation; broad/global availability to multiple specialized processors; long-range workspace architecture.
UCT-recoverable primitives: Content→consumer causal-access vector; breadth/coverage; persistence; macrostate/attractor transition; reachability.
Required bridge B_T: Content chart; preregistered consumer family; workspace coarse-graining; access metrics/thresholds; anatomical implementation for strong GNWT.
Strong target-theory claim preserved: Conscious access arises when local information is amplified/sustained and globally available through workspace dynamics.
Residual set R_T^res: Specific PFC/parietal timing, onset/offset, synchronization/content-coding predictions; empirical claims challenged/tested independently.
Explicit fidelity-failure condition: Fail if consumer family/access threshold/workspace grain are redefined per instance or if generic reachability is substituted for source-faithful ignition/global availability.

Canonical source: Brown, Lau & LeDoux 2019, Trends Cogn Sci, 10.1016/j.tics.2019.06.009
Distinctive signature Σ_T: A conscious first-order mental state is represented by an appropriate higher-order state; higher-order representation is not reducible to generic confidence/metacognition.
UCT-recoverable primitives: Higher→lower target sensitivity; downstream use; structural tracking; candidate representation relation.
Required bridge B_T: Mental-state chart; representation/aboutness grounding; theory-specific HOT form and content constraints.
Strong target-theory claim preserved: Higher-order representation plays the constitutive/explanatory role for conscious mental states.
Residual set R_T^res: Full representational semantics; HOT-specific architecture and phenomenal sufficiency/necessity claims; empirical localization/timing.
Explicit fidelity-failure condition: Fail if causal tracking is relabeled as semantic higher-order representation without an independent representation/aboutness bridge.

Canonical source: Hodson, Mehta & Smith 2024, Neurosci Biobehav Rev, 10.1016/j.neubiorev.2023.105473; Pezzulo et al. 2024
Distinctive signature Σ_T: Generative model; latent causes/beliefs; prediction/error structure; precision; variational inference; action/policy coupling; preferences/expected objectives for active inference.
UCT-recoverable primitives: Agent/environment response relations; model-state dynamics; prediction/error loops; policy-conditioned trajectories; formal F/G functionals after p/q/policy are fixed.
Required bridge B_T: Agent boundary; model semantics; pθ/qφ identification; latent variables; policies/preferences; learning-horizon rule.

Explicit fidelity-failure condition: Fail if pθ/qφ, latent-state semantics, precision, policy or preference structure are chosen post hoc to force a fit, or if alternatives are not compared.

Canonical source: Aru, Suzuki & Larkum 2020, Trends Cogn Sci, 10.1016/j.tics.2020.07.006

Canonical source: Budson et al. 2022, Cogn Behav Neurol, 10.1097/WNN.0000000000000319; Budson & Paller 2025, 10.2147/NSS.S522975
Distinctive signature Σ_T: Explicit-memory system as the system responsible for conscious perceptions, thoughts, memories, imaginings and dreams; temporally assembled/postdictive conscious stream.
UCT-recoverable primitives: Causal retention; multisource temporal assembly; memory→current-state influence; delayed integration.
Required bridge B_T: Working/episodic/semantic memory charts; encoding/retrieval/assembly definitions; content identity across time; empirical delays.
Strong target-theory claim preserved: The explicit-memory system is responsible for all conscious experiences.
Residual set R_T^res: Universal explicit-memory identity; detailed timing/postdictive claims; sleep/dream architecture; neuroanatomical memory-system claims.
Formal status F: temporal causal retention F4; theory F3; strong identity F0 given nonuniversality witness
Explicit fidelity-failure condition: Fail if generic temporal retention is called memory without independent memory-system identification, if the strong all-experience identity is deleted, or if F0 is asserted without a declared-domain token lacking the target explicit-memory system.

Canonical source: Graziano & Webb 2015, Front Psychol, 10.3389/fpsyg.2015.00500; Wilterson et al. 2020, 10.1016/j.pneurobio.2020.101844

UCT-recoverable primitives: Attention allocation variable; schema tracking; compression/model relation; schema→future attention causal control.
Required bridge B_T: Attention chart; representation/model grounding; control objective; self-model/awareness-attribution interpretation.

Residual set R_T^res: Semantic aboutness; awareness-attribution phenomenology/report; AST-specific control predictions.
Explicit fidelity-failure condition: Fail if generic feedback/control is substituted for a schematic attention model, or awareness-attribution semantics are silently assumed.
